name: run-mate-script-runner
description: Run package.json scripts (and Deno tasks, Makefile targets, just recipes) from the status bar. Finds nested projects and picks the right package manager, shell and Node version for you.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with RunMate
walkthroughs.description: Run your project's scripts with one click. Five short steps.

steps.title: Run a script
steps.description:
RunMate reads the scripts of your project and shows them as buttons in the status bar, the thin bar at the bottom of the window.

Click a button to run a script. Click it again to stop it.

[Open the script list](command:run-mate-script-runner.showAllScripts)

steps.title: Arrange the list your way
steps.description:
Every row in the script list has small buttons: move it up or down, star it, hide it.

The status bar follows the same order, and favorites get the first buttons.

[Open the script list](command:run-mate-script-runner.showAllScripts)

steps.title: Run with arguments, an env file or another shell
steps.description:
The terminal button on a row opens **Run with options**: add arguments such as ``--watch``, choose an env file such as ``.env.staging``, or run once in another shell.

Use it again quickly with **Run Last Script Again**.

[Run the last script again](command:run-mate-script-runner.runLastScript)

steps.title: Start several scripts with one click
steps.description:
A group is a button that starts several scripts together, for example the frontend and the backend.

You can share a group with your team, so everyone gets the same button.

[Make a group](command:run-mate-script-runner.newGroup)

steps.title: RunMate looks after the boring parts
steps.description:
The right package manager, the right folder, the right Node.js version, a free port. If something is missing or in the way, RunMate tells you and offers to fix it.

[Open RunMate settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22%40ext%3ASanekxArcs.run-mate-script-runner%22%5D)

run-mate-script-runner.statusBarLayout.markdownDescription:
What RunMate puts in the status bar (the thin bar at the bottom of the window).

- `auto`: decides for you. One project: a button for each script. Several projects: a button for each project.
- `scripts`: always a button for each script.
- `projects`: always a button for each project. Click it to see the scripts of that project.
- `picker`: just one "Scripts" button that opens the full list.

run-mate-script-runner.maxDynamicScriptB.markdownDescription:
How many scripts get their own button in the status bar. The rest stay one click away, behind the `...` button.

Example: with `3`, a project with 10 scripts shows 3 buttons and `... +7`. Set `0` to show only the `...` button.

run-mate-script-runner.maxProjectButtons.markdownDescription: How many projects get their own button when the status bar shows projects. The other projects stay reachable through the `...` button.

run-mate-script-runner.statusBarSide.markdownDescription: Which end of the status bar the buttons sit on. Try `right` if the left side is crowded.
enumDescriptions: Left end of the status bar.
Right end of the status bar.

run-mate-script-runner.useDynamicScriptP.markdownDescription: Show RunMate buttons in the status bar. Turn this off to hide all buttons; the script list still opens with `Ctrl+Alt+Q`.

run-mate-script-runner.nestedProjects.markdownDescription:
Also look for projects inside subfolders, not only in the folder you opened.

Example: you open `my-app`, and it contains `apps/web/package.json` and `apps/api/package.json`. With this on, RunMate shows `web` and `api` as separate projects and runs their scripts from their own folders.

Monorepo packages listed in `workspaces` (package.json) or in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` are found however deep they are.

run-mate-script-runner.nestedProjectsMax.markdownDescription:
How many folder levels down RunMate searches for projects.

Example: `apps/web` is 2 levels, `apps/web/tools` is 3. Raise the number if a project is not found.

run-mate-script-runner.nestedProjectsExc.markdownDescription: Folder names RunMate never looks into when it searches for projects. Add a folder here if it shows up as a project and should not (for example `examples`).

run-mate-script-runner.scriptSources.markdownDescription:
Which kinds of runnable things RunMate shows.

- `npm`: the `scripts` in `package.json` (also used for pnpm, Yarn and Bun projects)
- `deno`: the `tasks` in `deno.json`
- `make`: the targets in a `Makefile`
- `just`: the recipes in a `justfile`

Remove an item to stop seeing it. Example: `["npm"]` shows only package.json scripts.

run-mate-script-runner.workspaceMode.markdownDescription:
Only matters if you opened **several folders in one window** (a multi-root workspace). With a single folder, ignore this.

- `first`: read only the first folder.
- `all`: read every folder.
- `pick`: read every folder, show a script once even if several projects have it, and ask which project to run it in.
enumDescriptions: Every folder; ask which project when several have the script.

run-mate-script-runner.excludeScripts.markdownDescription:
Script names RunMate ignores completely: no button, not in the list.

To only tidy the list, use the eye button in the script list instead. Hidden scripts can be brought back from there; excluded ones only by editing this setting.

run-mate-script-runner.scriptOrder.markdownDescription:
The default order of scripts. Names listed here come first, in this order; all other scripts follow alphabetically.

If you move scripts with the arrow buttons in the script list, your own order wins over this setting.

run-mate-script-runner.shell.markdownDescription:
The shell (terminal program) that runs your scripts.

`default` uses the same shell as a new VS Code terminal. Choose another one if a script only works in a specific shell, for example Git Bash on Windows.

If the chosen shell is not installed, RunMate uses the default one. You can also choose a shell for a single run from the script list.
enumDescriptions: Same as a new VS Code terminal.

run-mate-script-runner.nodeVersionManage.markdownDescription:
Which tool RunMate uses to switch Node.js versions.

A project can ask for a Node version in `.nvmrc`, `.node-version`, `.tool-versions`, `volta.node`, or `engines.node` in `package.json`. If the Node that is active is a different one, RunMate switches to the right one for that run. If it already fits, nothing is switched.

- `auto`: use whichever tool is installed.
- `nvm`, `fnm`, `volta`: use only this one.
- `none`: never switch; always use the Node that is active.
enumDescriptions: nvm (macOS, Linux) or nvm for Windows.

run-mate-script-runner.preflightChecks.markdownDescription:
Before a script starts, check that what it needs is installed, and offer to install what is missing: the Node version the project asks for, a Node version manager, or the package manager (pnpm, Yarn, Bun).

RunMate always asks first and shows the command it will run. Turn this off if you never want to be asked.

run-mate-script-runner.autoInstallMissin.markdownDescription:
If the dependencies of the project are not installed yet (there is no `node_modules` folder), run the install command first and then the script.

Example: you clone a repository and click `dev`. RunMate runs `npm install` and then `npm run dev`.

run-mate-script-runner.alwaysInstallDepe.markdownDescription: Run the install command before **every** script, even when dependencies are already installed. Slower, but you never run with outdated packages.

run-mate-script-runner.reuseTerminalForS.markdownDescription: On: each script keeps one terminal tab and reuses it on every run. Off: every run opens a new terminal tab.

run-mate-script-runner.askBeforeKill.markdownDescription: When you start a script from the list while it is already running, ask whether to restart it or stop it. Off: restart it straight away.

run-mate-script-runner.checkPorts.markdownDescription:
Before starting a dev server, check that its port is free.

Example: you click `dev`, but an old server still sits on port 3000. Instead of a confusing error (or the server quietly moving to port 3001), RunMate tells you which program holds the port and offers to stop it.

RunMate knows the port from `--port 3000` / `-p 3000` / `PORT=3000` in the script or its arguments, from `PORT` in the chosen env file, or from the usual port of the tool (Vite 5173, Next.js 3000, Angular 4200, Astro 4321, Storybook 6006, and others). For anything else, use **Script Ports**.

run-mate-script-runner.scriptPorts.markdownDescription:
Tell RunMate which port a script uses, when it cannot work it out by itself. The name of the script on the left, the port on the right.

Example: `{ "dev": 8080, "api": 4000 }`

Used only by **Check Ports**.

run-mate-script-runner.notifyOnFailure.markdownDescription:
When a script stops with an error, show a message with **Run again** and **Show terminal** buttons.

The button of a failed script turns red in any case; this setting is only about the message. Stopping a script yourself is never reported as a failure.

run-mate-script-runner.envFile.markdownDescription:
An env file whose variables are loaded for **every** script, for example `.env.local`. Empty means none.

The file is looked for in the folder of each project. A project that does not have it runs as usual.

To choose an env file for **one** script (for example `dev` with `.env.staging`), open the script list, click the terminal button on its row and choose **Run with an env file...**. That choice wins over this setting.

Good to know: variables from the file are set in the terminal before the script starts, so they override the values your framework reads from its own `.env`.

name.description: The text of the group's button.

anyOf.description: A script of the project in the workspace root, for example "dev".

path.description: Folder of the project, relative to the workspace folder, for example "apps/web". Leave out for the root.

script.description: Name of the script, for example "dev". For other sources add the kind: "make:build", "just:up", "deno:start".

run-mate-script-runner.pickerOnly.markdownDescription: Old setting. Use **Status Bar Layout** = `picker` instead.
